name: Paraneoplastic Cerebellar Degeneration

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Diagnostic Criteria for Paraneoplastic Neurological Syndromes (PNS) 2004

criteria.description: Subacute onset of cerebellar ataxia progressing over weeks to months
Presence of an underlying malignancy known to be associated with PCD (e.g., small cell lung cancer, breast cancer, ovarian cancer)
Detection of well-characterized paraneoplastic antibodies (e.g., anti-Yo, anti-Hu, anti-Tr)
Exclusion of other causes of cerebellar degeneration such as toxic, metabolic, infectious, or hereditary etiologies

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Subacute cerebellar ataxia with confirmed underlying malignancy and exclusion of other causes; presence of onconeural antibodies supports diagnosis
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Early diagnosis is critical for management; antibody testing and cancer screening are essential.

pathognomonic.notes: Rapidly progressive gait and limb ataxia
Slurred or scanning speech due to cerebellar involvement

common.notes: Involuntary eye movements associated with cerebellar dysfunction

occasional.notes: Sensory or motor deficits in peripheral nerves
Mild memory or executive function deficits
Depression or anxiety related to illness
Difficulty swallowing due to cerebellar or brainstem involvement

rare.notes: Occasional seizures reported in some cases
Orthostatic hypotension or other autonomic symptoms

laboratory: Presence of onconeural antibodies (anti-Yo, anti-Hu, anti-Tr)
CSF analysis showing mild lymphocytic pleocytosis and elevated protein
imaging: MRI brain may show cerebellar atrophy in later stages

distinguishingFeatures: MRI lesions in CNS white matter
History of toxin exposure (e.g., alcohol, drugs)

redFlags: Rapidly progressive cerebellar symptoms over weeks
Presence of known malignancy or suspicious cancer symptoms
references: Graus F, et al. A clinical approach to diagnosis of autoimmune encephalitis. Lancet Neurol. 2016 Apr;15(4):391-404.
Darnell RB, Posner JB. Paraneoplastic syndromes affecting the nervous system. Semin Oncol. 2006 Apr;33(2):270-98.
Shams'ili S, et al. Paraneoplastic cerebellar degeneration associated with anti-Yo antibodies: a clinical analysis of 55 anti-Yo positive patients. Brain. 2003 Feb;126(Pt 2):1409-18.
